explanation: Poppies bloomed on the churned-up battlefields of Flanders, inspiring John McCrae's 1915 poem 'In Flanders Fields'. McCrae was a Canadian army doctor.

claims.text: The red poppy is worn in many countries to remember those killed in the First World War and later conflicts.
The rose, carnation and tulip are not the flowers worn for war remembrance.
Poppies grew on the disturbed ground of the battlefields of Flanders.
John McCrae wrote the poem 'In Flanders Fields' in 1915.
John McCrae was a Canadian army doctor.
